phases.name: Prepare
phases.goal: Have a stable bench and official setup resources ready.

steps.text: Choose the printer's final level surface and check the bench can carry the full setup.
Consider a paver only if it suits the bench and vibration problem.
Install the stock slicer and bookmark official assembly and support guidance. Save creator links for later; leave firmware unchanged.

phases.name: Unbox and inspect
phases.goal: An assembled printer with completed stock initialization, ready for first-print preparation.

steps.text: Save the serial number, order details and photos of the contents.
Photograph the pogo contacts and dock couplings on all four heads; ask support about any visible damage.
Assemble the printer using the official Quick Start Guide

actions: Use the Quick Start Guide or initial-setup video linked from the official U1 page. Follow the assembly sequence before turning to printing or modifications.
guidance.done_when: The assembly checklist is complete, with no loose, damaged or uncertain components.
guidance.if_stuck: Stop on damage or an unclear assembly step. Ask official support before powering or moving the printer.

sources.creator: Snapmaker
sources.note: Official U1 Quick Start Guide and initial-setup video

steps.text: Complete the on-screen first-start setup and stock calibration

actions: Use the official setup guide for the stock-firmware update and first-start sequence. Complete the requested calibration and build-plate handling on screen.
guidance.done_when: The setup and calibration sequence finishes without an unresolved warning.
guidance.if_stuck: Keep the printer stock and record the message if initialization fails; do not jump ahead to a test print.

sources.creator: Snapmaker
sources.note: Official U1 Quick Start Guide and initial-setup video

phases.name: First prints on stock firmware
phases.goal: Prepare a file, load filament and check your first stock prints. Useful modifications can wait.

steps.text: Choose a U1-ready first print file

actions: Use a U1-compatible local demo if available. Otherwise choose First layer test – STL from the official pre-flight guide below, or use a simple model you already trust.

In Snapmaker Orca, select matching U1/nozzle/material presets, import the model and choose Slice Plate. Slicing turns the model into printer instructions; an imported project may carry another printer’s settings.
Note which materials and toolheads the job needs before printing.
guidance.done_when: You have a U1-compatible sliced job and know which heads and materials it uses.
guidance.if_stuck: If no suitable local file is available, use the official slicer walkthrough below. Do not print another printer’s pre-sliced instructions.

steps.text: Load PLA for the first print

actions: Use the illustrated guide to match feeder and head. For PLA/PETG, trim a slanted end, mount the spool to unwind from below, then insert filament into the feeder.
A steady white light means preloaded, not loaded at the nozzle. Confirm material/color on Filament; set these manually for a non-RFID spool. If already Loaded, edit its information without reloading.
Choose Filament > Loading Mode, select that filament and tap Load. After extrusion and cleaning, tap Done. Repeat for other heads when needed.
guidance.done_when: Each required head shows Loaded with the correct material.
guidance.if_stuck: Do not force filament or start the print while loading fails. Use the loading-failure guide below. TPU has a different loading route; follow the linked manual-loading guide.

sources.creator: Snapmaker
sources.note: Manual loading route for flexible filament

steps.text: Check the build plate and filament mapping

actions: Confirm the build plate is installed as the setup guide requires and the print area is clear.
Review the job’s filament mapping: every selected toolhead must match a loaded spool of the intended material. Resolve mismatches before starting.
guidance.done_when: The file, actual loaded materials and selected heads agree, with no unresolved setup warning.
guidance.if_stuck: Cancel the start if the material, nozzle preset or mapping is uncertain. Correct the setup using the linked U1 printing guide.

sources.note: Stock first-layer checks; ask support before advanced adjustments

steps.text: Start the prepared print and stay nearby

actions: For a local job, use Start on the touchscreen and select the prepared file. Review its mapping and on-screen preferences.
For Snapmaker Orca over LAN, first put printer and computer on the same network. Enable Settings > LAN Mode on the U1, add the printer in Orca by IP/search, and confirm the request on the printer.
After slicing, use Upload and Print when ready. Upload alone transfers a file without necessarily starting it.
guidance.done_when: The intended job starts and you can observe its initial moves.
guidance.if_stuck: If connection or transfer fails, follow the official connection guide below. Stop if the displayed job differs; do not bypass warnings.

steps.text: Watch the first layer before leaving the printer

actions: Stay beside the printer for its first layer. Watch whether material stays on the plate instead of collecting on the nozzle or being dragged around.
guidance.done_when: The initial paths stay attached and motion proceeds without scraping, collisions or a repeated warning.
guidance.if_stuck: Pause or cancel a failing print. Keep hands clear of the moving/hot parts, save the message or a photo, and use official support for a new-machine fault.

sources.creator: Snapmaker
sources.note: Stock first-layer checks; ask support before advanced adjustments

steps.text: Let the plate cool before removing the print

actions: After the job finishes, wait for the bed to return to room temperature before removing the part.
guidance.done_when: The finished part is removed after cooling and the plate is ready for the next check.
guidance.if_stuck: Do not force a stuck part from a hot plate. Follow the plate’s own care guide if it will not release.

steps.text: Run a single-color print from each of the four toolheads; count an earlier single-color print if already done
Run one four-color print with a prime tower and watch the swaps, parking and loading.
Record idle fan noise and labelled temperature readings after a sustained print. Resolve failures with support before proceeding.

phases.name: First printed mods
phases.goal: Fit useful printed parts after clean stock tests.

steps.text: Review the split waste chute if emptying the stock collector is awkward.
Review a deflector wall if scraps miss the collection bucket.
Review the riser model and its cover fit; lighting is optional and priced separately.
Review tube supports, radius guides and any required fittings.
Find and credit the exact TPU holder model before printing; the imported source still needs review.
Choose tool holders and spool adapters for the parts you actually own; confirm each original model's hardware list.
Repeat vibration calibration after the riser or base changes.
Optionally review Build-sheet holder: two versions for your setup.
Optionally review Elegant spool holder for your setup.
Optionally review Original Hinge door-access mod for your setup.

phases.name: Firmware decision
phases.goal: Make a deliberate firmware choice after stock burn-in is clean.

steps.text: Stock first, mods second: stock tests help isolate a new-machine fault and preserve useful support evidence. From Day 4, consider extended firmware only if those tests are clean; staying stock is valid.
If proceeding, read the creator's current installation and stock-recovery guide before installing anything.
On compatible extended firmware, review the built-in camera option.
Optionally connect an existing Spoolman setup; StartHere hosts no service.
Optionally set print notifications through the firmware's own integration.
Review remote-access options only if you need them and accept the external service requirements.

phases.name: Dry-feed and tune
phases.goal: Use appropriate filament preparation and repeatable profiles.

steps.text: Buy a dryer only when needed; the checklist's four-spool choice is a priced option.
Route dryer tubing with gentle bends. When distant spools lose RFID detection, set each feeder's profile manually.
Dry PETG and TPU according to the filament maker's settings; record time and temperature with the spool notes.
Use a small VFA test before trying speed or wall-order changes.
Calibrate flow and pressure advance for the filaments you use, then save named profiles.
Review converted 3MF objects, tool assignments and prime-tower stability in the slicer before printing.
Optionally review Rear outlet for Sovol / Comgrow SH02 dryer for your setup.

phases.name: Expand when needed
phases.goal: Defer major purchases and machine changes until a real job justifies them.

steps.text: For an ABS/ASA trial, choose one appropriate enclosure route and review ventilation first.
After week one, review electronics cooling only with a complete documented route and suitable skills.
Do not add active chamber heat until motherboard cooling and enclosure prerequisites are satisfied.
Explore Full Spectrum's visual blending separately from hardware expansion for more filament slots.
Keep the original stock-test records and add your configuration changes to your maintenance notes.
Optionally review Cyberdyne vented IKEA top-cover adapter for your setup.
Optionally review Carbon + HEPA housing for an IKEA enclosure for your setup.
Optionally review Tareku mainboard / PSU cooling brackets for your setup.

milestones.complete_text: First-print preparation checks are marked. Start the prepared job and watch the first layer.

milestones.title: Stock baseline checked
milestones.complete_text: Stock-test checks are marked. You can keep printing; hardware and firmware changes are optional.
